name: Phases of Guard
description: Work out when to build connections, attack, or recover your guard. Use concrete cues and positional rounds to change priorities before a pass settles into a pin.
summary: Guard play shifts between making connections, using them to attack, and recovering them when a pass threatens.
overview: The engagement, maintenance, and retention framework appears in Rob Biernacki and Stephan Kesting’s BJJ Formula curriculum. Use it to choose your next job; a live exchange can move between these priorities within a few seconds.
key_takeaways: Engagement: make a useful connection without letting the passer move straight around your legs.
Maintenance: use grips and hooks to affect posture or balance while keeping a way to follow the passer.
Retention: when the passer clears your legs or wins an angle, protect the space around your torso and recover a barrier.
Change priorities when the position changes. A lost grip matters less than a passer who has already reached your hip.
Offense can help retention when it restores control or balance; abandon an attack that leaves you unable to follow the pass.

bjj_applications.scenario: Seated, facing a standing passer without grips
bjj_applications.application: Stay facing the passer and seek a connection you can use, such as wrist control with a foot or shin managing distance. Do not lie back expecting an absent grip to hold them nearby.
bjj_applications.outcome: You have a starting point for a guard rather than a named position with no control.

bjj_applications.scenario: Your De La Riva hook and grips are established
bjj_applications.application: Use your connections to move the passer’s weight and test a sweep. Follow their stance changes; the hook alone does not keep the guard intact.
bjj_applications.outcome: The passer has to address your balance threat while you check which connections remain useful.

bjj_applications.scenario: The passer clears your feet and reaches the side of your hips
bjj_applications.application: Release an attacking grip if it prevents you from framing. Face the passer, keep your elbows near your knees, and make room to bring a leg back between you.
bjj_applications.outcome: Recovering any workable guard gives you another chance to establish your preferred one.

common_mistakes.mistake: Insisting on the original guard after its grips and angle are gone
common_mistakes.consequence: You keep searching for an attack while the passer reaches your torso.
common_mistakes.correction: Recover a frame or leg first; choose the guard once you have space.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating the phases as a fixed sequence
common_mistakes.consequence: You pause to complete a label even when a sweep or recovery is already available.
common_mistakes.correction: Use the labels after the round to explain a decision, not as commands that override the position.

training_exercises.name: Three starting points
training_exercises.description: Start one exchange disconnected, one in an established open guard, and one with the passer beside the legs but without a chest pin. Bottom tries to sweep or recover; top tries to pass. Reset on a sweep, a settled pin, or a tap, then change the starting point.
training_exercises.focus: Recognize the job imposed by the starting position.

training_exercises.name: Replay the lost connection
training_exercises.description: After a pass, agree on the first grip, hook, or angle that bottom lost. Restart just before that moment at manageable resistance. Try a recovery instead of continuing the original attack; reset when guard returns or the pin settles.
training_exercises.focus: Notice the cue to switch from attacking to recovering.

knowledge_assessment.question: Your attacking grip remains, but the passer has cleared both legs. What changes?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The urgent job is protecting your torso and recovering a barrier. Keep the grip only if it helps that job.

knowledge_assessment.question: Does retention always mean abandoning offense?
knowledge_assessment.answer: No. A balance threat may help you recover, but the attack must leave a workable answer to the pass.
